title: Before Evidence Can Decide: Candidate-Set Formation, Discovery Routing, and Unconceived Alternatives — Questions for a Pre-Evidential Epistemology of Science

equations.section: 2 A Minimal Cycle, Not a Solution
equations.meaning: Candidate-set operator mapping the readout-distinguishable hypothesis classes reachable by an epistemic system to the live candidate set actually entering comparison/pursuit/test planning.

equations.section: 2 A Minimal Cycle, Not a Solution
equations.meaning: Comparative appraisal typed as a map from the live candidate set, declared records, and appraisal policy to a ranking/rejection/acceptance/pursuit/abstention/revision outcome.

equations.section: 2 A Minimal Cycle, Not a Solution
equations.text: H not in C_{E,t}(Q)  =>  H receives no comparative appraisal at cycle t
equations.meaning: Definitional consequence: a hypothesis outside the live candidate set is not evaluated at that cycle, without implying it is true, superior, or permanently unavailable.

equations.section: 2 A Minimal Cycle, Not a Solution
equations.meaning: Evidence can alter the next candidate set by changing the retained problem, question, reader, or access geometry.

equations.section: 2 A Minimal Cycle, Not a Solution
equations.meaning: The full cycle is a loop, not a wall between discovery and justification.

equations.label: (Q5, unlabeled)
equations.section: 4.5 Q5. What is the collective candidate set?
equations.meaning: Posed and questioned candidate hypothesis that a group's live collective set is simply the union of members' private sets; the paper answers 'probably not in all cases' (communication, prestige, role assignment, shared instruments, and meeting structure can prevent or exceed simple union).

equations.text: Question -> Candidate-set formation -> Appraisal -> Record -> Candidate-set revision
equations.meaning: Restated research-agenda loop; the open problem is what determines the middle-left arrow (candidate-set formation).
